contract.request: No business parameters needed. Protected REST negotiation, Bearer, identity, collaborator-owner mapping and scoped reference checks precede method and role handling. Ordinary checkout does not parse unused payload; scoped impersonation still validates it.
contract.response: Association scope returns 410 with existing msg: Software subscriptions are no longer required. OPTIONS retains authenticated metadata.
contract.errors: Non-association scope returns 403 msg=Info not available. Missing/invalid/inactive/deleted Bearer remains 401. Admin/impersonation/resource denials retain 403. Method 405, Accept 406, format 404 and malformed-session HTML 500 retain precedence. Scoped checkout invalid JSON returns 400 before tombstone.
contract.authentication: Bearer required; session and BKN_AUTH cookies do not authenticate REST. Existing session/audit reader runs before transport.
contract.permissions: Both routes are excluded from collaborator permission registry, but owner availability/mapping still applies. Administrator must impersonate. Association-scoped athlete cannot access these operations; scoped collaborator references remain guarded.
contract.resource_scope: Legacy role check uses resolved ScopeUser, not initiating actor. Plan state cannot grant access or change response.
contract.side_effects: No entitlement/payment/provider work. All managed model snapshots, including prepared legacy plans/subscriptions, remain unchanged after both servers. Valid/malformed session bytes remain unchanged in fixtures; shared invalid-hash session revocation remains possible.
contract.transaction: No business writes or billing SELECTs. Pure service chooses role-dependent tombstone from admitted scope. Query tracing forbids legacy billing-table reads.

evidence: 10 portable methods first pass on Django ASGI and fail against unregistered Go routes, then pass on both real servers. Missing/expired/cancelled/paid/no-expiration plan fixtures retain 410. Role/scope, method/metadata, session, scoped-vs-unused body handling and 32 concurrent requests are covered. Managed-table and session-byte readback is unchanged; cleanup restores preexisting state.

PostgreSQL race integration passes: one/two SELECTs for current-account admission, zero additional service queries and no legacy billing-table queries. Thirty-two mixed calls use 40 SELECTs within four test database connections. This is not full middleware query accounting or a performance improvement claim.

CORS root increment: 51 portable HTTP methods per backend across five policies and 32 declared Python URL comparisons pass on actual Django ASGI/Uvicorn and Go controlled terminals. Four additional methods pass on both actual application roots with managed-model/session readback unchanged. Preflight precedes routing/session/auth and still works on five Go paths with PostgreSQL/Redis unavailable. The environment oracle now passes 79 declarations including existing CORS settings/defaults/proxies. Evidence: quality-reports/go-migration/cors/; contract and remaining global middleware/debug/stream/proxy limits: BE_GO/internal/middleware/cors.md.

Security header increment: six portable methods per backend compare current Django SecurityMiddleware defaults against Go, with explicit/empty response fields, all HTTP methods/statuses, streaming, forwarded protocol and 32 concurrent requests. Five actual-root methods verify health/authentication/CSRF/method/not-found responses and CORS preflight bypass. No new configuration or HSTS/redirect/frame policy is introduced. See BE_GO/internal/middleware/security_headers.md and quality-reports/go-migration/security-headers/. Complete global middleware/restore/proxy parity remains open.

Production runtime correction: BE/Dockerfile pins Python 3.13.2. The previous local 3.12.6 URL expectations accepted malformed bracketed origins; CI 3.12.15 rejected them. Forty declared URL comparisons and 51 portable CORS methods now pass on production Python 3.13.2 and Go; all 40 URL expectations also pass in the shipped-style Django image. JSON trailing-comma diagnostics now use the production array/object messages and comma positions, including Unicode and whitespace. CI and the full accounts adapter require the exact Dockerfile interpreter. Existing TESTS/adapters/django/runtime.py remains the disposable Docker adapter; the new version guard is production_runtime.py.

Restore HTTP admission: 42 portable methods per backend across open, queued, running, exclusively locked, unavailable-volume and disabled-path modes pass on real Django ASGI and the compiled Go root. The existing DATA_RESTORE_LOCK_PATH flock and global queued/running instance_datarestore receipts fence ordinary work before security/session/auth; original exemptions and CORS precedence remain. Managed model/cache bytes stay unchanged. Real PostgreSQL checks one SELECT per unsafe admission over 1/16/128/512 receipts, no pending query for GET/HEAD, 32 concurrent admissions in a four-connection pool, and the existing one_active_data_restore partial-index plan. Cross-process tests prove Django/Go exclusion and SIGKILL lock release in both directions; in-flight HTTP and panic release pass. The environment oracle passes 87 declarations. Evidence: quality-reports/go-migration/restore-admission/; scope and remaining full restore/task/scheduler/stream gaps: BE_GO/internal/service/restore_admission.md.

The complete current accounts adapter passes on production Python 3.13.2 with restore/CORS/security composition, all existing account/scope/login/image/audit checks and managed-state readback. Evidence: quality-reports/go-migration/restore-admission/full-accounts-production.log and full-accounts-results.json. Bidirectional credentials, permissions, provider protocols, cache/rate/security adapters, Go race/vet, health/recovery and the non-root Linux image rehearsal also pass. Current-model fixtures do not prove historical migrations, browser switching or complete backend parity.
notes: Intentional current-main retirement: software subscription gating and platform checkout stay disabled. Existing HTTP tombstones remain required for old clients; association/course memberships, payments and communications are not deprecated.

Existing TESTS access, initial-import, lifecycle and manual contracts require the active-plan 410, but those complete browser/lifecycle workflows are not proved against Go by this isolated endpoint rehearsal.

Portable differential compares full responses, selected headers, publisher requests, unchanged records/cache and bounded SQL. At 16/128 sections owner reads use two SQL statements and collaborator reads three. Whole Go vet/race passes.

Actual Django/Go processes serialize refresh under the same file lease, including cancellation; changing the Go lock filename fails the test. Packaged Go/Django filesystem probes pass both shared-volume initialization orders as UID 10001 with read-only roots; the previous Go image fails Go-first. All private probe resources removed. These checks do not claim packaged HTTP refresh or a verified required release artifact.

Unchanged built frontend passes real password login and manual navigation/search/reload/authenticated-image/mobile/denial checks with Django and Go, using the same authored synthetic corpus and 640x360 PNG. Exact consumed image Blob hashes and dimensions are checked; screenshots inspected. Pinned pre-route Go f2993b0 fails with an actual manual-sections 404. Private canonical API proxy only; root WebSockets remain Django. Existing profile/audit checks also pass. See docs/architecture/go-migration/manual-reader.md for scope.

contract.request: Required email query parameter; last duplicate wins; no trimming or syntax validation. Unicode character limit 255; get_user presence enables details and username fallback.
contract.response: 200 valid=true with data.msg; 409 valid=false with exception. get_user returns first_name,last_name,email,user_id of smallest UUID email match; only if absent, smallest UUID username match.
contract.errors: 400 invalid payload for excessive length; missing query retains production HTML 500 without Allow. Supplied Bearer and scoped identity are checked before method/query. 401/403/405/406 and format 404 retain existing REST behavior. Malformed session fails before method/Bearer with generic HTML 500.
contract.authentication: AllowAny with supplied Bearer authentication. Cache session supplies audit identity only. Anonymous forged scope headers are ignored.
contract.permissions: Current identity/scoped-operation admission; association-bound athlete denied; excluded from collaborator permission registry.
contract.resource_scope: Intentionally global public identifier lookup. Case-insensitive PostgreSQL comparison; excludes soft-deleted accounts, includes inactive accounts. Not a business-resource authorization repository.
contract.side_effects: Read-only checks; managed-table and malformed-session-byte readback unchanged after both real HTTP servers. General shared session middleware may revoke invalid password-hash sessions.
contract.transaction: No business writes. Email performs one SELECT and at most one fallback SELECT; username SELECT EXISTS. Context cancellation and repository failures propagate, never become availability.

evidence: 16 portable HTTP methods first passed on actual Django ASGI and failed against the unregistered Go routes, then pass on both real servers. Controlled inactive/deleted/duplicate/literal fixtures, Unicode bounds, options/errors, actor/scope/session precedence and 32 concurrent requests have explicit expected results. All managed models remain unchanged.

Real PostgreSQL integration passes under the race detector: 1/16/128/512 duplicates preserve one-query smallest-UUID selection, fallback uses two queries, username uses one EXISTS. Thirty-two concurrent calls stay within four test connections; cancellation and closed database fail correctly. EXPLAIN ANALYZE captures actual query text: email sequential scan/top-N sort, username sequential scan within EXISTS. No latency or scan-complexity improvement claimed.

CORS root increment: 51 portable HTTP methods per backend across five policies and 32 declared Python URL comparisons pass on actual Django ASGI/Uvicorn and Go controlled terminals. Four additional methods pass on both actual application roots with managed-model/session readback unchanged. Preflight precedes routing/session/auth and still works on five Go paths with PostgreSQL/Redis unavailable. The environment oracle now passes 79 declarations including existing CORS settings/defaults/proxies. Evidence: quality-reports/go-migration/cors/; contract and remaining global middleware/debug/stream/proxy limits: BE_GO/internal/middleware/cors.md.

Security header increment: six portable methods per backend compare current Django SecurityMiddleware defaults against Go, with explicit/empty response fields, all HTTP methods/statuses, streaming, forwarded protocol and 32 concurrent requests. See BE_GO/internal/middleware/security_headers.md and quality-reports/go-migration/security-headers/. Complete global middleware/restore/proxy parity remains open.

contract.request: POST JSON/form/multipart: username+password without token selects password admission; username+token+backend selects social admission, even with password present. Raw values and OTP presence are preserved for ordered service validation.
contract.response: The root composes session/rate/REST admission and credential/response/finalization services. Forty-one password/social HTTP scenarios prove declared response bodies and signed-token/cookie delivery, including an avatar. Sixteen password and sixteen cross-identity social requests pass concurrently per backend. Full image registry and all supported input/resource/transport behavior remain incomplete.
contract.errors: Credential/OTP and social selection error precedence is characterized. Unknown account returns 401 invalid credential (not found); ambiguous/inactive selection 401 invalid credentials. After candidate selection: unsupported backend 400, invalid social token 401, email mismatch 401, non-string provider email server error. Missing/wrong-length OTP returns 401 OTP code required.; six-character mismatch returns 401 OTP code not valid.; non-sized OTP or corrupt secret reached during verification raises a server error. The registered handler maps these errors. Focused actual-server tests verify password/OTP denials and generic 500 failures without token/cookie delivery; broader provider/input failures remain open.
contract.authentication: AllowAny still authenticates supplied Bearer credentials. Existing cache-session audit precedes shared IP/account rate limits, then REST negotiation, Bearer/scope and body admission. Nineteen ordinary and five rate-ordering methods, sixteen password and sixteen cross-identity social concurrent requests pass on actual servers. Remaining global middleware, historical credential/resource and provider transport gates remain incomplete.
contract.side_effects: Password stage: all matching obsolete Django hashes are upgraded, including ambiguous/inactive outcomes; raw bcrypt only migrates the selected candidate before active-status rejection. Username normalization now creates the existing user update audit and optional association index before OTP; OTP denial retains those writes. Actor and logging-in account remain separate. Membership-card response construction now reads the lowest-UUID existing configuration or creates a default plus create audit and direct association index. Superusers/athletes do not create configurations; collaborators use their connected owner. A separate finalization service atomically updates last_login and cancels current/future UTC delete_on with User audit/index; it is wired into the public HTTP workflow. Declared effects are read back using Django; complete failure/race parity remains open.
contract.transaction: Go credential stage uses bounded keyset pages and batched writes inside a repeatable-read snapshot; only actual password writes lock rows; expected denials commit documented upgrades, infrastructure failures roll back. Serialization/deadlock conflicts retry at most three times. Django partial writes on exceptional failures are deliberately replaced by this atomic boundary. Whole-login transaction coordination remains open. Username/audit/index writes use a separate row-locked atomic transaction with at most three deadlock/serialization retries. This deliberately rolls back orphan pre-save audits that Django can leave after a username uniqueness failure; exact failure-side-effect parity is not claimed. Configuration/audit/index creation is an explicit read-committed transaction with a scoped parent lock and at most three conflict retries; finalization has its own row-locked user/audit/index transaction; whole-login composition is wired, while cross-runtime creation coordination remains open.

evidence: 21 explicit Django actual-view versus Go service account-selection/password-write cases using production hashers; Django verifies Go-written hashes and all managed model tables are compared after restoring declared test changes. This is credential-stage evidence, not portable Go login HTTP parity.

47 explicit second-factor decisions from the actual Django login view versus Go service at fixed PyOTP times. Includes Unicode, adjacent-window denial, malformed values/secrets, multipart metadata, disabled 2FA and current replay semantics. Django token identity and denial last-login behavior are checked; managed tables are compared after declared fixture resets. This is not a Go login HTTP endpoint.

20 actual Django login/audit-middleware versus composed Go password/preparation/OTP cases; exact username/event/index fields and Django readback, with all managed tables unchanged after fixture restoration. Real PostgreSQL checks prove atomic failure rollback, five queries for indexed normalization, one for unchanged names, 32 concurrent calls without duplicate events, and retry after a forced cross-actor deadlock.

46 explicitly expected Django-rendered base profile versus Go cases on the same private PostgreSQL; all managed tables unchanged after declared fixture restoration. One/two SELECTs regardless of 0/1/2/128/512 onboarding rows; 32 concurrent association reads use 64 SELECTs and release the four-connection pool. Current preference transitions, cancellation and no-partial-profile behavior are tested. This is component evidence, not portable login HTTP parity.

Real PostgreSQL denied-SELECT roles prove optional onboarding failure returns the complete base profile with null onboarding, while required association group failure returns no profile. Both boundaries are characterized through Django; Go releases the aborted transaction and reuses the pool.

23 explicitly expected association profile JSON/outcome cases compare Django serializer/DRF rendering with Go on the same private PostgreSQL. All 50 fields, exact decimal text, PostgreSQL scale rounding, null/scalar JSON, reviewed boundary and deleted/inactive owner semantics are checked. Group counts 0/1/16/128/512 use two SELECTs; 32 concurrent 512-group reads use 64 SELECTs. A deletion/restoration transition is immediately visible; all managed tables match after restoration.

20 explicit actual Django login-response-builder/audit middleware versus Go membership-card cases; exact configuration/audit/index fields and Django readback. Existing/duplicate rows use two statements, creation five; 32 concurrent Go calls create one invariant in 67 statements. Real permission/FK failures, injected errors, cancellation and an observed PostgreSQL audit-actor deadlock verify rollback/retry. Every managed table and SQL-NULL distinction matches after resets.

17 explicit actual Django password-login versus Go finalization cases cover UTC deletion-date boundaries, exact last_login and audit/index readback. Two/four/five-statement paths, 32 concurrent Go calls in 67 statements, real permission/FK failures, injected failures and cancellation verify atomicity and pool release. Django partial autocommit and stale-save overwrites are characterized separately; all managed tables match after restoration.

36 explicitly expected actual Django builder versus Go composed-response cases on shared private PostgreSQL, including all key presence, role-0 behavior, feature masks, exact JSON settings, instructor cardinalities 0/1/2/128/512 and default configuration write/readback. Existing association/collaborator responses use seven statements; creation ten; 32 concurrent compositions use 224 statements on four connections. Real required-instructor permission failures and persisted transitions are tested; all managed tables match after restoration. Image conversion is deliberately outside these cases. Twenty-eight boolean values and eight dotenv cases are characterized with Django and checked in Go.

Image prerequisites: ten explicitly expected actual-Django-helper size decisions, 54 exact Pillow pixel vectors across six modes and 19,535 CPython Base64 differential vectors pass. Go matches every pixel byte without tolerance, preserves immutable inputs and passes cancellation, logical memory/overflow limits and 32 concurrent transformations. All managed tables remain unchanged. The 54 transformed rasters also match their encoded JPEG bytes. JPEG pixel decoding is covered separately; these checks do not provide the complete image processor.

180 exact Pillow JPEG vectors cover five modes, four deterministic patterns and nine sizes. Metadata/quality/sampling expectations anchor the oracle. Input/output limits, exact output ceilings, malformed native protocol, process failure, environment isolation, timeout, queued/running cancellation and 32 concurrent encodes pass. The shipped static codec also passes the same 180 vectors and native protocol in the actual non-root, read-only, networkless Go image. Tested libjpeg-turbo versions: Pillow 3.1.0, local 3.2.0, image 3.0.4; no other codec/architecture equivalence is assumed.

JPEG decoder: 312 exact pixel/comment cases and 1,556 explicit invalid streams; the actual Django compress_base64 helper agrees on all 1,868 output/fallback cases. Of the decoded cases, 310 re-encode byte-exactly and two preserve long-comment save failure. Progressive/optimized/sampling/RGB/CMYK/YCCK/restart/metadata cases, tolerated corruption, every incomplete prefix of selected baseline/progressive streams and comment ordering/size boundaries are covered. Native framing, exact raster budgets, process failure, queued/running cancellation, timeout and 32 concurrent decodes pass. The shipped non-root read-only/networkless codec passes the same cases. Native sanitizer checks assert exact exit codes and complete frames, so generic error mapping cannot conceal failures. Other formats and full image-service parity remain open.

Lazy JPEG marker phase: 1,352 explicit Pillow recognition outcomes, covering all marker codes, payload truncation, precision/component/quantization semantics, metadata marker checks, comments, pixel warnings/hard limits, ordinary encoded headers and prefixes across the first SOS boundary. Three actual Django header-only passthrough cases retain the original despite undecodable pixels. Go checks consumed-header budgets, immutable/non-aliased metadata, EXIF/comment ordering, MPF offsets, scanning cancellation and 32 concurrent readers. The image rehearsal runs the same marker oracle. Raw metadata retention alone is not full Image.open admission; the subsequent metadata stage is covered separately.

JPEG metadata: 226 explicitly expected EXIF/MPF first-frame outcomes, exact JPEG bytes, directory/record cancellation and 32 concurrent MPO inspections. Complete JPEG file pipeline: 73 explicit disk-size/lazy/fallback cases plus all metadata and 1,868 decoder cases; actual Django helper and shipped non-root read-only/networkless image agree. Per-stage logical budgets, 32 concurrent resizes and whole-pipeline queued/running cancellation with child reaping and admission reuse pass. Other file formats and public login remain open.

PNG compressed pixels: 803 explicit cases compare independently constructed samples with Pillow across 15 depth/color combinations, five filters, Adam7, large buffers and malformed streams. Actual Django helper results distinguish 480 exact unchanged-size JPEG outputs, 300 unsupported-mode fallbacks and 23 invalid-stream fallbacks. Go checks pixel/transform/JPEG composition, exact logical budgets, overflow, mid-decode cancellation and 32 concurrent Adam7 decodes; the non-root read-only/networkless image runs the same oracle. Valid zlib stream ends on complete ordinary/Adam7 rows leave remaining pixels zero; incomplete rows or missing trailers before remaining rows still fail. These cases cover pixel composition; file-level metadata/canvas behavior is covered separately.

PNG lazy header/metadata: 394 explicit Pillow outcomes cover chunk/CRC and metadata payload rules, text inflation/cumulative character ceilings, duplicate headers, APNG frame declarations/sequences/rectangles and text-key collisions. The actual Django helper returns original URIs for 235 valid 200x100 headers with zero pixel loads observed through a delegating loader. Exact consumed-header budgets, metadata ownership, cancellation during text inflation/conversion and 32 concurrent readers pass; the non-root read-only/networkless image runs the same oracle. File-level validation and canvas composition are covered separately; public image wiring remains open. Mode-1 transforms preserve accumulated-coordinate nearest-neighbour rounding: 210 exact pixel/JPEG vectors and 18 actual Django PNG size-policy cases pass, with exact budgets, invalid samples, ownership, cancellation and 32 concurrent transforms/encodes. The shipped non-root read-only/networkless image runs these checks. IDAT boundaries require separate handling because concatenation changes Pillow checksum/error timing. The PNGStreamDecoder now preserves per-chunk/64 KiB reads and row-limited native zlib inflation across 852 explicit cases (803 existing pixel vectors plus 49 chunk cases), comparing pixels and consumed-file position/remainder/sequence. Exact logical budgets, malformed native protocol/frames, timeout, running/queued cancellation, child reaping/admission reuse, mid-unpack cancellation and 32 concurrent decodes pass. The shipped non-root read-only/networkless image runs the same oracle and native protocol, with zlib version/license delivery. ASan/UBSan checks require exact successful frames, invalid-input exit 2/no output and no diagnostics; 18 additional malformed-protocol/budget cases also check exact exits under both builds. This stream evidence alone does not establish file-level admission. The composed PNGFileProcessor now matches 1,466 explicitly expected whole-file JPEG/original decisions against Pillow and the actual Django helper, including cumulative pre/post text accounting, post-pixel CRC/header/payload rules, inherited comments and RGBA comment removal, first/later fdAT sequences, original animation/mode/size semantics, zero extents and Adam7 origin placement across all 15 mode/depth combinations. The shipped non-root read-only/networkless image runs the same oracle. Stage budgets, exact tail/canvas limits, mid-tail/canvas cancellation, immutable input, 32 concurrent pipelines and encoder-stage running/queued cancellation with child reaping/admission reuse pass. Other formats, dispatch, shared admission and public image/login composition remain open.

Exact stage budgets, invalid specifications, input ownership, mid-header/raw/RLE cancellation, 32 concurrent pipelines, queue timeouts and encoder-stage cancellation/reaping/admission reuse pass. Other formats, dispatch/shared admission and public image/login composition remain open; no endpoint is newly verified.
